about: Where the port may differ from .NET Framework's System.Drawing, and why. DrawingParityTests: in a case matching 'case', the lines matching 'line' (the golden's and the port's) are set aside; what remains must be equal. An entry that sets aside no difference (on its platform: 'all', 'windows' or 'linux') fails the test: it is stale; but for 'varies': what .NET Framework gives there changes from run to run, and may happen to equal the port's. None is the port's own doing: each is .NET's System.Drawing.Common (Microsoft's package on Windows does the same), .NET's runtime, or .NET Framework's undefined behaviour.

differences.reason: The system colors: Windows reads the user's theme; Linux has none, and .NET's System.Drawing.Primitives (the runtime's, not the port) gives fixed ones (Windows XP's). SystemBrushes and SystemPens are of those colors.
Windows' icons (SystemIcons, a file's associated icon from the shell): the Unix implementation has none, and gives one placeholder icon for all.

Printing: the Unix implementation (Mono's) asks CUPS, with its own defaults, collections and checks; no printer in the container (Windows has its print-to-PDF ones). Web applications do not print on the server.

Geometry is libgdiplus': it flattens curves into other points (an ellipse from the other side), bounds a region by its rectangles as given (GDI+ by the pixels it covers), and does not implement GraphicsPath.Widen and Warp (the path is only flattened).
Metafiles: libgdiplus reads an EMF's records (not EMF+: GDI+'s dual metafile reads as Emf, its header so), draws them partly, and neither enumerates nor records them (NotImplementedException).

Not in libgdiplus or the Unix implementation (NotImplementedException): writing several frames (SaveAdd: a multipage TIFF, an animated GIF), an adjusted palette, the halftone palette, a Win32 resource, rendering to a device context, a font from a device context.
Windows' device contexts, windows and bitmap handles (HDC, HWND, HBITMAP) and the screen (X11): none on a Linux server. What GDI+ answers for a null handle, the Unix implementation answers otherwise.

The fonts installed: Liberation (fonts-liberation2: Arial's metrics as Liberation Sans) and DejaVu, not Windows' (Arial, Bahnschrift...). fontconfig gives Liberation Sans for new Font("Arial"), but a font collection has only its own names.

libgdiplus' and the Unix implementation's own answers: SetResolution flags the image (HasRealDpi), BitmapData's reserved field, thumbnails and texture images in 32bppArgb (GDI+: premultiplied), Clone's error for a format it cannot convert to (ArgumentException, GDI+: OutOfMemoryException), the sigma bell blend's points, a line cap of both a fill and a stroke path (GDI+ refuses it), properties on a bitmap made in memory (libgdiplus keeps them for files' formats only), a toolbox bitmap found in the component's resources.

What libgdiplus says of a picture it read: no HasRealDpi flag, a PNG's resolution as 96 (GDI+: 95.9866, from pixels per meter), a turned JPEG still Jpeg (GDI+: MemoryBMP), the EXIF tags libexif adds (resolution, versions) without the JPEG tables GDI+ lists, a GIF's first frame delay only (GDI+: every frame's), a thumbnail in 32bppArgb.
Color.DarkSeaGreen is #8FBC8F on .NET (CSS's value), #8FBC8B on .NET Framework: .NET's System.Drawing.Primitives (the runtime's), not the port.
An invalid CopyPixelOperation: the same InvalidEnumArgumentException, naming the parameter ("copyPixelOperation") where .NET Framework says "value".
A scale out of [0, 1]: the same ArgumentException, which .NET gives its ParamName ("scale").

A bilinear warp: gdiplus.dll's own result changes from call to call, even in one .NET Framework process (the points it flattens the curves to; a NaN point at times): memory it reads before writing. The port passes the same arguments to the same GdipWarpPath.
A handle that is no icon: ArgumentException on both, .NET's with the runtime's message and ParamName ("handle").
ImageFormat.ToString of a format made from a known GUID: .NET names it ("Png"), .NET Framework only for the static instances ("[ImageFormat: b96b3caf-...]").
Setting DllName to a relative path: .NET Framework demands a FileIOPermission for it (Code Access Security, which .NET does not have) and fails; .NET sets it.

For an EMF, .NET Framework reads these past what GdipGetMetafileHeaderFromMetafile writes (its ENHMETAHEADER is 100 bytes, GDI+'s 88): memory never written, another value every run. The port zeroes the buffer first (Metafile.Windows.cs): 0.
A pen with no pattern, and an empty pattern set: the same exceptions (OutOfMemoryException, ArgumentException) with .NET's messages.
Ending a page or a job never started: .NET Framework throws NullReferenceException (a null DC), .NET checks and does nothing.
Copying into too short an array: the ArgumentException of the runtime's Array.Copy, whose message and ParamName .NET changed.

SupportsColor: .NET Framework asks the bits per pixel of an information context for the printer (GetDeviceCaps(BITSPIXEL) > 1: InvalidPrinterException for a printer that does not exist, true for many monochrome ones), .NET asks the driver (DeviceCapabilities(DC_COLORDEVICE); its default, false, for no printer).
The large (32x32) image: .NET Framework fails (Parameter is not valid) for a resource without one, .NET scales the small one.
